items.title: The internal Hom from the structure sheaf of an effective Cartier divisor is the conormal sheaf shifted by one
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter duality.tex (Duality for Schemes)

items.difficulty_reason: For a scheme X and an effective Cartier divisor D in X, the lemma asserts a canonical isomorphism RSheafHom(O_D, O_X) = N[-1] in D(O_D) (statement lines 3367-3373). The proof reformulates this as the statement that RSheafHom(O_D, O_X) has a unique nonzero cohomology sheaf in degree 1 isomorphic to N, and since the pushforward i_* is exact and fully faithful it suffices to prove the assertion after applying i_* (proof lines 3375-3383). Lemma labelled lemma-sheaf-with-exact-support-ext identifies i_*RSheafHom(O_D, O_X) with RSheafHom_{O_X}(i_*O_D, O_X), and the short exact sequence 0 -> I -> O_X -> i_*O_D -> 0 for the ideal sheaf of D computes it: using RSheafHom_{O_X}(O_X, O_X) = O_X and a local computation RSheafHom_{O_X}(I, O_X) = O_X(D), one gets RSheafHom_{O_X}(i_*O_D, O_X) = (O_X -> O_X(D)) with O_X in degree 0 and O_X(D) in degree 1 (proof lines 3384-3400). The result then follows from the short exact sequence 0 -> O_X -> O_X(D) -> i_*N -> 0 that comes from D being the zero scheme of the canonical section of O_X(D) and from N = i^*O_X(D) (proof lines 3400-3406). Computing the internal Hom through the ideal sequence and then reading off the degree one part is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
